sections.name: TestItCannotRunPerProcess
sections.title: Single process cannot run
sections.what: Checks that the reconciler cannot run on one process, since that would always look clean. It requires at least two records, and only the reduce module may build the reconciler. No loop may build it.
sections.why: The docstring says one process compared with itself always looks clean, which hides problems.
sections.watch_out: Building the reconciler in a new place, or inside a loop, will fail these tests on purpose.

sections.name: TestComputedNotAsserted
sections.title: Computed facts not asked of model
sections.what: Checks that the model is never asked which processes share an enabler, or whether cycles exist. The code reads attributions from the records, and splits weights by effort so they sum to one. An unshared enabler yields no attribution, and the model is routed to the defensible tier.
sections.why: The docstrings say a model would miss attribution lookups and would claim no cycles when there are some.
sections.watch_out: If either field returns to the model's output, the model is again asked to compute facts the code can compute.

sections.name: TestCycleDetection
sections.title: Cycle detection checks
sections.what: Checks the cycle finder on simple graphs: none, a chain, a diamond, a two-step loop and a three-step loop. Also checks that a loop makes the plan unschedulable and an acyclic plan is schedulable.
sections.why: Reason not stated beyond the test names. A cycle means work cannot be put in a valid order.
sections.watch_out: A diamond shape must not count as a cycle, or valid plans get blocked.

sections.name: TestCalibration
sections.title: Calibration bounds and refusals
sections.what: Checks the model never gives a raw score, and that the raw score is read from the process record. An adjustment may move a score by at most two from that real score, clamped to zero to five. Adjustments naming an unknown process or dimension are refused, as are two adjustments on one dimension.
sections.why: The docstring describes an earlier defect where the model chose its own starting score, so the limit bounded the wrong number.
sections.watch_out: The bound is measured from the record's score, so changing the record's source changes the result.

sections.name: TestBoundary
sections.title: Capacity findings and weight arithmetic
sections.what: Checks that capacity findings pass through with their function and concern. Also checks the weight arithmetic lives in the value package, not in the reconciler's source.
sections.why: The docstring says sums and divisions are rollups, which belong to code.
sections.watch_out: The source check is a text search, so rewording the code can make it pass or fail for the wrong reason.

sections.name: TestTheGraphComesFromTheRecords (part 1)
sections.title: Dependency graph built from records
sections.what: Checks every declared prerequisite becomes an edge, every prerequisite kind maps to a reason, process-to-process ordering is mapped, and a self-dependency is reported rather than crashing. Declared edges also reach the final result.
sections.why: The docstring says a model restating declared dependencies would drop some, which could hide a cycle.
sections.watch_out: Every new prerequisite kind must map to a reason, or these checks fail.

sections.name: TestTheGraphComesFromTheRecords: test_a_cycle_through_a_declared_prerequisite_is_detected
sections.title: Cycles from declared prerequisites
sections.what: Checks a loop declared in the records is found even though the model is never asked about it. Also checks a model edge that repeats a declared one is dropped, and an unmappable self-dependency is recorded as a warning.
sections.why: The docstring says the earlier design could not see cycles declared in records.
sections.watch_out: Duplicate edges would make the graph look denser and could create false cycles.

sections.name: TestTheDeltaIsBoundedAgainstTheRecord (part 1)
sections.title: Raw score absent from schema
sections.what: Checks the raw score field is absent from the judgement model and from the full schema the model sees. A further test rebuilds a model with that field added back and confirms the check catches it.
sections.why: The docstring says the raw score was once on the model output, letting the model choose its own baseline.
sections.watch_out: Removing or weakening this check would let the field return without notice.

sections.name: TestTheDeltaIsBoundedAgainstTheRecord: test_reintroducing_raw_score_is_refused_rather_than_ignored
sections.title: Raw score cannot be smuggled in
sections.what: Checks the judgement model rejects extra fields, so a raw score cannot be passed in directly. Then sweeps every raw score from zero to five against every delta from minus two to two, confirming the calibrated score stays within two of the record and within zero to five. Also checks the record itself is not changed.
sections.why: The docstring says forbidding extra fields stops the field returning through a side door.
sections.watch_out: The expected values depend on the clamping rule, so changing that rule changes these checks.

sections.name: TestTheCapacityCheck
sections.title: Capacity check status reporting
sections.what: Checks the capacity check reports not_run without headcount by function, and establishment_read when headcount is given. An empty headcount is treated as none. Also checks headcount reaches the model, and that the model is told not to report findings when headcount is missing.
sections.why: The docstring says an empty findings list alone cannot tell checked-and-clean from never checked.
sections.watch_out: The status establishment_read does not mean a comparison ran, so do not read it as one.

summary: Tests the portfolio reconciler, the stage that works across all processes at once, and checks that it cannot run on a single process and that its rules hold for shared prerequisites and capacity.
purpose: Covers the reduce step, which compares processes against each other. Only the first eight sections are described here; the file has more tests covering cycles, calibration, boundary checks, and capacity.
why: Likely reason: the module description says the key test is that the reconciler cannot be called with one process, because its job only makes sense across a portfolio.
how: Builds sample process records and prerequisite edges, then provides helpers that inspect the output schema for field names and build records with a chosen prerequisite. The later tests in the file use these helpers.
inputs: Sample process records, prerequisite edges, and adjustment judgements, plus a stub client.
outputs: Pass or fail results for the tests in the file. No real model calls.
risks: The helpers depend on how the sample records are built. A change in the shared record builder could change many results at once.
debug: If a helper-based test fails, check the sample record builder first, then the schema field names the helper reads.
